ordered_diagnoses: Tall cell variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction with highly vascularized mass
salient_findings: Voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
Hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Considerable uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy regarding rib and vertebral lesions
key_facts: Woman in her 30s with no relevant medical history
Progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction
Voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
Endoscopic examination found a highly vascularized mass
CT scan showed a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity, left thyroid, fifth rib, and L4 vertebra
MRI confirmed a hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Radioiodine scintigraphy found considerable uptake regarding rib and vertebral lesions
Serum thyroglobulin significantly elevated at 4432 ng/mL
Biopsy results confirmed VTC metastasis

raw.rationale: The presence of distant metastases in the ribs and vertebrae, as well as the highly vascularized nature of the tumors, is more consistent with follicular thyroid carcinoma, which has a higher propensity for hematogenous spread compared to other types of thyroid cancer.

rejected.label: Papillary thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: Papillary thyroid carcinoma tends to spread through lymphatic channels rather than hematogenously, which does not align with the distant metastases found in this case.

rejected.label: Medullary thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: Medullary thyroid carcinoma is less likely given the lack of mention of elevated calcitonin levels or other specific markers for this disease.

rejected.label: Tall cell variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: While aggressive, tall cell variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma would not typically present with the pattern of distant metastases seen here without significant lymph node involvement.

rejected.label: Hürthle cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Hürthle cell carcinoma is a variant of follicular thyroid carcinoma but is less common and the clinical presentation does not specifically suggest this subtype over follicular thyroid carcinoma.

rejected.label: Papillary thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: The vascular nature and sites of metastasis are less typical for papillary thyroid carcinoma
